## D1. This repository is the genome (2026-10-30; status: accepted, confirmed by owner 2026-10-30)
- **Context:** Skills were kept as zip uploads and a Mac folder; improvements made in one harness did not reach the others, and there was no history.
- **Decision:** The marketplace repo `Horef/claude-plugins` holds the source of every skill and mod. Installed or uploaded copies are read-only "phenotypes", rebuilt from it. Local clones are where agents write.
- **Alternatives:** one repo per skill - more overhead, and cross-skill lessons have no common home; a Drive folder - no history, no review, no CI.
- **Consequences:** sharing is a link to the marketplace; every harness needs a way to reach a clone (the `genome` config file) or to hand observations back.
- **Evidence / source:** owner's request (2026-10-30 session).

## D2. Observations as one-line Markdown, not a database or symbols (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The owner offered that agents could think "in strange symbols" if other agents can read them.
- **Decision:** `LEARNINGS.md` holds one plain-language line per observation with a small fixed grammar (id, date, kind, section, text, ×count, → version), parseable by `loop.py`, writable by hand in any harness.
- **Alternatives:** a JSONL/SQLite store - needs tools in harnesses that have none; a dense symbolic code - unusual glyphs cost extra tokens, are harder to grep, and models reason in words anyway; the gain would be aesthetic, not functional.
- **Consequences:** human-readable diffs and reviews; the format is checked by `loop.py check`.
- **Evidence / source:** design reasoning; ACE itemised bullets with ids (docs/RESEARCH.md §2).

## D3. Evidence gate before rule changes (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** Research found that self-generated skills give no average gain and LLM-written AGENTS.md can lower success while raising cost.
- **Decision:** Only verified fixes change a unit immediately. Rules change from ripe observations (seen twice, or a verified failure) and must keep the unit's evals passing per case. Reading a skill produces observations, not rewrites.
- **Alternatives:** let agents rewrite skills freely - context collapse and drift; require a human for every change - the maintenance burden the owner wants gone.
- **Consequences:** the system improves more slowly but does not regress silently; seed observations from adoption wait for confirmation by use.
- **Evidence / source:** SkillsBench, Gloaguen et al. 2026, ACE, SkillOpt (docs/RESEARCH.md §2-3); established for the first two, abstract-level for SkillOpt.

## D4. A fixed kernel the loop cannot change by itself (2026-10-30; status: accepted, confirmed by owner 2026-10-30)
- **Context:** Self-improving systems have gamed their own checks (DGM removed hallucination markers; STOP tried to disable its sandbox).
- **Decision:** strange-loop's kernel rules, change classes and ripeness thresholds change only with the owner's approval; graders and the graded never change in the same commit.
- **Alternatives:** model reviewers only (Ouroboros-style quorum) - moves the trust problem up a level; no protection - known to fail.
- **Consequences:** the owner is consulted rarely, but on exactly the changes where self-assessment is least reliable. The owner asks agents to raise a kernel change with him when they see the need (2026-10-30).
- **Evidence / source:** docs/RESEARCH.md §3; GEB's "inviolate level"; Suber's Nomic.

## D5. Portable core, harness adapters at the edge (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The owner uses Claude Code, claude.ai, Kiro and Copilot; some agents see one skill or one folder only.
- **Decision:** The protocol is Markdown plus stdlib Python, readable without any plugin. Harness-specific parts are optional adapters: the Claude Code session-start digest hook; `claude plugin eval` for with/without comparisons; the "Observations for <unit>" reply block for chat-only harnesses.
- **Alternatives:** an MCP server or a hook-only design - would not reach claude.ai skills or Kiro.
- **Consequences:** the weakest harness still participates; the strongest get automation.
- **Evidence / source:** project-foundations principle "portable tooling only"; agentskills.io standard (docs/RESEARCH.md §5).

## D6. The genome runs project-foundations on itself, with plugin-repo exemptions (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The genome needs the same continuity (STATUS, WORKLOG, DECISIONS, checks) as any project, and running a skill on its own home is its best test.
- **Decision:** docmap runs from the skill's own `scripts/docmap.py` with `docmap.toml`; plugin and skill folders are README-exempt (their SKILL.md and README describe them), and model-router's TS files are header-exempt for now.
- **Alternatives:** no project scaffolding - agents lose continuity between sessions; full docmap rules - noisy READMEs inside every skill (project-foundations O4).
- **Consequences:** `docs/MAP.md` is nearly empty; the value is in check, the decision index and doc lifecycle.
- **Evidence / source:** first docmap run on this repo, 2026-10-30 (WORKLOG).

## D7. The sciencefig library lives inside the scientific-figures skill (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The library lived only on the owner's Mac; every claude.ai chat shipped it in as an archive and shipped changes back the same way, and other harnesses could not use it.
- **Decision:** `plugins/scientific-figures/skills/scientific-figures/lib/` holds the library, its benchmarks, assets and reconstructions, with `LICENSES.md`. It travels with the skill (plugin install, upload zip, clone).
- **Alternatives:** its own repository or pip package - a second thing to version and install, and skill and library could drift apart; keep it on the Mac - the archive round trip and no cloud use.
- **Consequences:** the upload zip is about 2 MB; the CC BY-NC-SA reconstructions are now in a public repository, allowed for non-commercial use with credit and the same licence, which `LICENSES.md` states; the Mac folder `~/Scripts/ScientificFigures` can be retired once the clone's evals pass there.
- **Evidence / source:** owner approved (2026-10-30); `evals/run.py` builds, lints and renders all 31 benchmark figures in a cloud container.

## D8. Plugins are labelled general or personal (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The owner shares the marketplace with other people. strange-loop, project-foundations and model-router are general by design (personal facts live in git-ignored or `~/.config` files); scientific-figures and course-lecture-notes are written for the owner's setup.
- **Decision:** Each marketplace entry carries `category: general | personal`, and the README lists the two groups separately. A general plugin must not contain one person's facts (they go in a local file the plugin reads); a personal plugin may.
- **Alternatives:** a second marketplace for personal plugins - two things to sync and maintain, and the loop is the same for both; making every plugin general now - a restructure of the owner's daily tools without evidence that anyone else needs them (proposed to the owner instead).
- **Consequences:** readers see what transfers; a personal plugin can later be generalised with the same person-layer pattern as project-foundations and move to `general`.
- **Evidence / source:** owner's question (2026-10-30); `claude plugin validate .` accepts the `category` field.

## D9. Personal choices live in a profile the skill reads (2026-10-30; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The owner asked to generalise scientific-figures (D8 listed it as personal). Its method and library were general; its audience, output target (DEVONthink notes with Anki prose) and preferences were one person's.
- **Decision:** A general skill keeps one person's choices outside its folder, in `~/.config/<skill>/profile.md` (template `profile.example.md` in the skill), or in the person's standing instructions where a chat app has no file access. Target-specific rules (e.g. DEVONthink) go in a reference file loaded when that target applies. Personal skills that depend on such a target load the reference directly. scientific-figures is now `general`.
- **Alternatives:** keep personal rules in SKILL.md behind "if you are Sergiy" - leaks one person's setup to everyone; a fork per person - two copies drift.
- **Consequences:** the same pattern as `AGENTS.local.md` in project-foundations; course-lecture-notes stays personal but now loads scientific-figures' DEVONthink reference itself.
- **Evidence / source:** owner's request (2026-10-30); scientific-figures 7.0.0 evals pass (31 figures) and two judged cases cover both paths.
